findings.message: On main, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md contain no chupa:core markers, and chupa's config routes both claude and codex. classify_core therefore returns `missing` for both files. This ticket ships core_drift as a hard gate in Check and in the inline and queued merge rerun. It explicitly leaves migration and docs out, and it fences neither conduct file. Phase 6 Deliverables call chupa's own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md 'the first case' of first adoption, but no registry row owns rendering and committing them. 19.P6.core-drift-activation also omits this fact. As a result, from the next drain onward, every ticket on this repo (starting with migrate-config, admitted in the same admission) fails core_drift before main moves. The only way out is an unplanned operator `chupa core` plus a hand commit of a section-17 render target. That is a hold with no planned release.
findings.paved_road: Repair 19.P6.core-drift-activation (Owner/Records/Observable) to name the owner and order for making the self-host's routed conduct current. One option: this deliverable fences CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md and commits their mechanical `chupa core` render, with a criterion that the gate classifies both as `current` on the branch, and test_core_first_adoption_preserves_project_bytes is adjusted to the rendered bytes. The other option: a predecessor row does this before activation. Also state how a mechanical core render interacts with CLAUDE.md being authored from section 17. Then re-author the ticket from the repaired unit.
